To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
obesity in dogs is associated to an enhanced alpha-2 adrenerigc antilipolytic response of fat cells.
the antilipolytic response to alpha-2 adrenoceptor activation is enhanced in fat cells from obese dogs and is dependent on the site from where the adipose tissue was sampled.
the antilipolytic response of dog fat cells to alpha-adrenergically mediated agonists is enhanced in obese animals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the alpha-adrenergics in the dog adipose tissue.
the study of the adrenergic control of lipolysis and with the mechanisms involved in the pathophysiology of obesity.
the study of the adrenergic control of lipolysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the alpha-2 adrenoceptors are the main mediators of the antilipolytic response to catecholamines in dog adipocytes, and that obesity in the dog is associated with an increased alpha-2 adrenoreceptor response.
the alpha-adrenergically mediated inhibition of lipolyses is a major determinant of the antilipolytic action of the catecholamines in the dog fat cells.
the dog adipocyte has an alpha 2-mediated antilipolylic effect that is enhanced in obese dogs and is stronger in subscutaneous than in omentum adipocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

alpha-2-adrenergic receptors are involved in the regulation of lipolysis, and the alpha-adrenergically-mediated inhibition is enhanced in large fat cells from obese dog, especially those from the subcutaneous tissue.
in the dog adipocyte the antilipolytic alpha 2-adrenoceptor effect is enhanced (or even unmasked) in the presence of a large adipocyte size and/or in subcutaneous adipocytes.
obesity in dogs, at least in part, is due to a modification in the alpha/beta balance in the dog adipocyte.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the alpha 2-mediated inhibition of lipolys is enhanced in large fat cells from obese dogs.
obesity and fat tissue localization are associated with a modification of the lipolytic response to alpha 2-adrenergic stimulation.
the alpha-2 adrenerigic response to epinephrin is enhanced in the obese dog fat cell.
